Campus Couriers is a peer-to-peer campus errand platform. Students can request items from campus suppliers and other students can pick them up and deliver them.
A student can use Campus Couriers in two roles: requester, when asking for an item to be collected, and courier, when accepting and delivering another student's errand.
You need to register and sign in before using the account-based parts of Campus Couriers.
Registration asks for your name, an NUS email address, and a password.
Campus Couriers accepts NUS email addresses, including common NUS subdomains such as u.nus.edu.
A registration password must be 16 to 128 characters and include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character.
After creating an account, you are returned to the sign-in page and can sign in with your new credentials.
The sign-in form uses your NUS email and password. If sign-in fails, the page shows an error message so you can try again.
After signing in, the main navigation lets you browse errands, view My errands, browse Suppliers, and create a new errand.
The application is designed to support complete requester and courier workflows on desktop and mobile screen sizes.
The Browse errands page shows open errands that are currently available for a courier to accept.
Each open errand card can show the requested item, pickup location, delivery location, credit value, and collection deadline.
The Browse errands page also shows your active errands, so you can quickly see requests you created or errands you accepted.
Use Refresh on the Browse errands page to reload open errands and active errands.
You can filter open errands by delivery location.
You can filter open errands by credit value: up to 5 credits, 6–10 credits, or 11 or more credits.
You can filter open errands by expiry: expiring in the next 4 hours, expiring today, or expiring in the next 7 days.
You can sort open errands by expiry time, either soonest first or latest first.
You can sort open errands by credit value, either highest first or lowest first.
If no open errands match the selected filters, choose Clear filters to return to the full available list.
If open errands cannot be loaded, the page explains that they are unavailable and provides a Try again action.
To accept an errand, select it from the open-errands list and confirm the acceptance in the confirmation dialog.
After you accept an errand, it is added to your active errands and you become responsible for collecting and delivering it.
An errand can be accepted by only one courier. If another courier accepts it first, the list is refreshed and you are told that it is no longer available.
A requester cannot accept their own errand.
The Suppliers page lets you browse campus suppliers and choose a supplier when starting an errand.
Supplier cards can show a supplier image, name, campus building, floor, category, and description.
If a supplier has no image, the supplier card displays a fallback visual instead.
Search suppliers by supplier name or campus location using the supplier search field.
Filter suppliers by category or by campus building.
Supplier results are paginated. Use Previous and Next to move between pages when more than one page is available.
The Suppliers page reports how many suppliers were found and shows a no-suppliers message when the search has no matches.
Select Create errand here on a supplier card to start a new errand with that supplier preselected.
The Create an errand page lets you request an item from a pickup supplier and specify where and how it should be delivered.
When creating an errand, choose a pickup supplier from the available supplier list.
Enter the requested items in the Requested items field. You can describe multiple items, for example, two sandwiches and one coffee.
Choose a delivery building from the available campus delivery locations.
Enter the delivery floor, such as 3.
Enter delivery instructions to help the courier find you, such as meeting outside a particular room and being messaged on arrival.
Choose a Collect before deadline for the errand.
Choose a whole-number credit offer of at least 1 credit for the courier.
The create-errand form shows your available credit balance. The credit offer cannot exceed the available balance.
When an errand is created, the offered credits are reserved and are transferred only after delivery is confirmed.
If the credit balance cannot be loaded, the form displays the problem and provides a Retry action.
The Create errand button is unavailable until required form information and a usable credit balance are present.

If required information is missing, the form identifies the field that needs attention, such as the pickup supplier, requested items, delivery building, delivery floor, delivery instructions, deadline, or credits.
After successful creation, the page confirms that the errand was created and displays its reference.
The My errands page lists errands that you requested or accepted.
Use the My errands filters to view All errands, only errands you are Requesting, or only errands you are Delivering.
Errands you request or accept appear in your active-errands summary and on the My errands page while they are in progress.
Each active errand can show its progress, credit value, requested item, pickup location, delivery location, and a link to view details.
Active errand progress can include Waiting for courier, Accepted, Waiting for requester, and Awaiting confirmation.
If you have no active errands, the application explains that errands you request or accept will appear there.
If your errands cannot be loaded, use the available Try again or Refresh action to reload them.
The errand details page shows a reference number, current status, credit value, pickup route, delivery location, delivery instructions, collection deadline, requester, and courier when assigned.
The route section identifies both the pickup supplier and pickup location and the destination building and floor.
If no delivery instructions were provided, the details page says that no additional instructions were provided.
The details page formats important timestamps such as creation time, acceptance time, collection deadline, and terminal outcome time.
An Open errand is waiting for a courier and remains visible to couriers until its collection deadline.
An Accepted errand has a courier assigned. For the requester, the page says a courier is assigned; for the courier, it says delivery is in progress.
A Completed errand is one whose delivery the requester confirmed as completed.
A Cancelled errand was canceled by the requester before it was accepted.
A Failed errand was reported as unsuccessful and is closed. The details page can show the reported problem.
An Expired errand was not accepted by a courier before its collection deadline.
A requester can cancel an Open errand from its details page, subject to the action being permitted.
When an errand is Accepted, the requester can use Confirm delivery after receiving the items.
The requester should confirm delivery only after receiving the requested items.
When an errand is Accepted, the requester can use Report problem if the delivery was unsuccessful and enter a reason for the problem.
After an action such as canceling, confirming delivery, or reporting a problem, the details page refreshes to show the updated status.
Use Refresh on the errand details page to retrieve the latest information.
The closed credit economy rewards couriers with platform credits for successfully completing errands.
Credits are reserved from the requester when an errand is created and transferred to the courier only after the requester confirms delivery.
If an errand is canceled or expires before completion, its reserved credits are released to the requester.
Platform credits are for use within Campus Couriers. They cannot be purchased, withdrawn, or exchanged for money.
The credit offer pays the courier for completing the errand; it is not payment to the campus supplier.
Payment for items bought from a supplier is outside the Campus Couriers platform.
Campus Couriers provides supplier and campus-location information, but it does not provide supplier menus, product catalogs, inventory, or checkout.
Campus Couriers does not provide live courier location tracking while an errand is being carried out.
When a page cannot load data, the interface shows a clear loading or error state and generally provides a Refresh, Retry, Try again, or Clear filters action.
A signed-in user can open an errand's details from an active-errand card or from the My errands list.
If a page or route does not exist, Campus Couriers shows a not-found page rather than the requested content.
